transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-24
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Huang (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM), Monica Reyes (Greenfield Head of ML), Jonah Pierce (Greenfield Infra), Aisha Khan (Greenfield Security), Evan Lee (Greenfield Data Ops)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to triage access blockers, review the last set of latency/throughput measurements, agree remediation actions for staging VPC peering and KMS handoff, and decide on next bench runs before pilot sign-off. Some background flakiness on long-tail latency; noticed a couple of cold-start outliers and one sustained 5xx run that correlated with gateway misrouting.

Topics:
- Staging access status and VPC peering
- KV cache warmup and cold-start behavior
- Latency outliers and 5xx incident on 11/22
- Security/KMS handoff items
- Next bench runs and acceptance criteria

Action items (recorded in meeting and mirrored above): see action_items metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: alright everyone, uh thanks for joining, we'll just run through status, quick triage on the long-tail latency, and then remediation plan. Marco and I can take notes. Monica, wanna kick us off with how the onboarding is looking from your side?
[00:18] Monica: yeah thanks, Samir. overall good progress, we got the staging creds Friday but we saw intermittent auth failures overnight, which Jonah has been looking at. still blocked from running the 10k token cold start test at scale because the gateway is dropping some of the sessions.
[00:32] Jonah: yeah to confirm, there were a couple of NAT gateway timeouts, and our LB healthchecks were routing to the instance with stale ip rules, so some packets were getting dropped. we've patched an iptables rule but want Redwood to validate the peer route - I sent a traceroute log earlier.
[00:45] Lina: I saw that log, Jonah — thanks. from our side the artifacts looked like typical VPC mis-route where the KV cache warm path isn't being hit for the first few requests. that explains the cold-start spikes we saw in the 11/22 run.
[01:02] Samir: okay good, that's consistent with what the bench showed. Marco, can you pull the bench snapshot?
[01:08] Marco: sure one sec, pulling up the csv - looks like median token latency is 180ms but p95 jumped to 1.2s on the 11/22 run and p99 hits 2.8s with a couple of 5xx spikes at minute 24.
[01:25] Monica: yeah that p99 is the real customer-facing metric for us, if it sits at 2.8 seconds for search flows it's going to be noisy.
[01:31] Evan: quick context: a lot of our load is bursty, e.g., report generation spikes at 03:00 ET so the long-tail really matters. we don't care about absolute median as much as the tail.
[01:45] Lina: two quick things - first, the KV cache policy we shipped defaults to 30s TTL on prefixes which is conservative; we can bump to aggressive warmup for staging and that materially reduces cold-start. second, we noticed the runtime had an occasional fallback to CPU for a micro-batch which increases token path by 3x for that request.
[02:07] Jonah: fallback to CPU? do you know why that happened, Lina?
[02:10] Lina: likely scheduler preemption — one of the nodes had a competing process, or the kernel scheduled a compaction job. it's rare but with bursts it lines up badly. we can lock CUDA affinity or reserve the node for the pool.
[02:22] Samir: that's where Dedicated would help, but for the pilot we can do pool constraints and pinning. Jonah, will you be able to allow port 6001 for the backplane and confirm peer routes after your NAT changes?
[02:34] Jonah: I can open 6001, yes. will also dump route tables and post to the thread.
[02:38] Monica: security note: Aisha, do we have any objections to opening that port?
[02:42] Aisha: we need to see the security posture: whether it's one-to-one peering or transit via a jump host. also KMS rotation window — we need to ensure Redwood can request a short-lived key or use our customer-managed key with the recommended policy.
[03:00] Samir: we support customer-managed keys and can integrate with your KMS. we asked for the rotation window earlier, and Lina's team can do a test sign/verify. Aisha, can you share the KMS policy snippet we need?
[03:12] Aisha: yes I'll post that after this call. one ask: we need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance with a 90-day retention. is that doable?
[03:22] Marco: we can send a formatted export and an ingestion guide, Redwood will provide the syslog endpoint example.
[03:26] Samir: noted, we'll share the logs export method - action item.
[03:28] Monica: back to the bench, Samir, what configuration did you run for the 11/22 test? was quantization involved?
[03:35] Samir: it was int8 quantized variant, default batch size 8, sequence length 1024, and a warmup of 100 requests. But our long-tail indicates warmup didn't hit due to session drop.
[03:47] Evan: can we run a synthetic with longer initial prefix to force KV warm? maybe a dedicated 500 warm prefix shots.
[03:53] Lina: yes we've been recommending an early prefix strategy for apps that have report generation; we'll add a synthetic warm-up vector in the bench script.
[03:59] Jonah: aside — I noticed one of the 5xx's coincided with an autoscaler event in our cluster around minute 23, the node joined late and some connections timed out.
[04:10] Samir: that aligns with CPU fallback too. For remediation: 1) we coordinate a bench run with fixed node reservations, 2) open the port and validate peer routes, 3) temporary aggressive KV warmup, 4) audit log/KMS handoff. any other high priority?
[04:26] Monica: can we also have a run that mimics our 03:00 ET spike? the burst pattern, not steady QPS.
[04:33] Lina: yep will parameterize burst profiles.
[04:36] Samir: great. Now, any security blockers preventing us from running the large long-duration bench in staging?
[04:41] Aisha: main blocker is the KMS integration and the SAML mapping for service accounts. we also need to confirm the IP allowlist for the Redwoods endpoints — sorry redwood endpoints - redwood, that's me mis-saying.
[04:55] Samir: no worries. We'll provide the endpoints we plan to use and can do the SAML mapping test in a separate window.
[05:02] Marco: quick note on costs — ramping warmup increases token counts in bench but reduces tail in production. we'll show cost delta in the bench csv so you can pick trade-offs.
[05:12] Monica: yes please include a cost per 100k sessions number. that's what procurement will ask.
[05:17] Samir: will do. Lina, can you describe the long-tail test you'll run?
[05:20] Lina: plan is three staged runs: (a) burst profile with aggressive KV warm policy (b) burst with default policy (c) long-hang test to capture late p99 at minute 30+. we'll capture system metrics and token breakdowns. expect each run ~45 min.
[05:36] Evan: question: what's the impact to our SLO if we accept p95 at 1s but p99 at 2.5s?
[05:42] Monica: for search we need p99 < 1.8s, so current numbers are above that.
[05:47] Samir: okay, let's target p99 < 1.8 for the next benchmark with warmup and reserved nodes.
[05:53] Jonah: I'll coordinate node reservations with infra and ensure autoscaler doesn't evict. one note: our staging budget is limited, so we may not be able to reserve forever, just during the bench window.
[06:03] Aisha: also please note we require attestation for SOC 2 scope items we discussed; Samir, you mentioned sending a security pack?
[06:10] Samir: yes, will email our SOC 2 summary, the data flow diagram, and the minimal KMS policy sample.
[06:15] Aisha: and a note on logging — we want to ensure PII is redacted before logs leave their network.
[06:21] Lina: Redwood's runtime has an option to mask tokens in trace exports; we'll enable that by default for your export.
[06:27] Monica: timeline — if we can clear the VPC peer route and KMS by Monday, then we can run the long-tail bench Tuesday/Wednesday and aim for a pilot acceptance decision by next Friday.
[06:37] Samir: sounds good. recap of owners: Samir to send bench CSV+cost delta and SOC2 pack; Jonah to post route tables and NAT logs; Aisha to post KMS policy and attestations; Lina to run three bench profiles and post results; Marco to prepare the bench analysis doc.
[06:55] Jonah: small ask — would Redwood consider a temporary increase in connection timeout to 90s while we hammer the staging bench? reduces retries on our side.
[07:03] Lina: we can add a config override in the gateway for that bench window. won't change production.
[07:09] Evan: perfect. any open questions?
[07:12] Monica: just one: competitor question — someone from procurement asked about Anthropic latency comparisons. Samir, do we have a short note?
[07:20] Samir: yes we'll include a comparison slide — but note comparatives vary widely by model and sequence length; we'll include equivalent bench numbers with same payload.
[07:29] Aisha: another security question — can we restrict outbound endpoints to your IP ranges only?
[07:34] Marco: yes we'll provide IPs and a recommended firewall rule set.
[07:38] Samir: okay time check, we have about 10 minutes left. let's pick a date for the coordinated bench: does Tuesday 2026-12-01 at 23:00 UTC work?
[07:48] Monica: that's 18:00 PT, works for us.
[07:51] Jonah: works.
[07:53] Aisha: works pending KMS snippet arrival.
[07:56] Samir: good, tentatively booked. final recap and next steps — I'll post the bench CSV and I will also share a lightweight runbook for the bench window with exact port and ip ranges. Lina will schedule the bench runs and post the results in the pilot board. Jonah and Aisha will confirm routing and KMS. Marco will deliver bench analysis.
[08:16] Monica: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:19] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up in thread.

End of transcript.
